*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the
social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf), please note that members of the
public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of September 1, 2020, at 2:00 P.M.
as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  C l e r k / S e c r e t a r y a t yhorton@cityofinglewood.org, a n d D e p u t y C i t y C l e r k
  aphillips@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  In Person: While adhering to and enforcing social distancing standards, members of the public can
  come to the Community Room located on the First Floor of Inglewood City Hall at 1 West Manchester
  Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301, to listen, observe and make public comments.

  3.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments by using the following:

  l Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 (Access Code: 5967569# (wait 5 seconds and press # again)):
  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5
  minutes prior. Should any person need assistance with audio, please dial 1-888-796-6118. When
  dialing in, the operator will provide further instructions on how you can make public comments via
  phone.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from
  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Facebook Live or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line,
  it is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone
  transmission. Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be
  inaudible due to feedback.

  4.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  l Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/.

Inglewood, California
  September 1, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
September 1, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

MAYOR PRO TEM APPOINTMENT. It was moved by Council Member Franklin,
and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby appoint
Council Member Morales as Mayor Pro Tem for Closed Session. The motion was
carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Franklin;
Noes:  None; and
Absent:  Mayor Butts.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01
p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Pro
  Tem Morales; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Pro Tem
Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Session Item No. CS-1.

127.1  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts

  EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 20-08 RATIFIED AND APPROVED – EXTENSION
  OF THE TENANT EVICTION PROTECTIONS. Initiative by Mayor Butts, dated
  September 1, 2020 recommending the ratification of Executive Order No. 20-08
  extending the Tenant Eviction Protections provided for during the COVID-19 emergency

  3
 to September 30, 2020.

Mayor Butts announced that Council Member Franklin mentioned the extension of the
tenant eviction protections and it was placed on the agenda. Mayor Butts also stated that
the Governor extended the State’s order until December.

Council Member Franklin corrected the State’s extension date to January 21, 2021.

Mayor Butts recommended an extension until January 31, 2021. He inquired of the City
Attorney, Kenneth Campos, if the City can be more restrictive than the State.
The Mayor also asked if the City didn’t require the 25% payment, as the Governor’s
order requires, would it be more or less restrictive than State Laws.

Kenneth Campos, City Attorney, reported that it was his understanding that the City
would have to follow the Governor’s order.

Mayor Butts, stated the order would be merited until January 21, 2021.

Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, reminded the Mayor that he previously gave the date of
January 31, 2021 for the extension of the tenant eviction protections order.

Mayor Butts, reported that the City Attorney recommended following the State’s order of
January 21, 2021, and if the City approved the date of January 31, 2021, it would require
more than a 25% payment.

Council Member Morales stated the City would adhere to the Governor’s order.

Mayor Butts reiterated that the City would follow the guidelines put in place from the
State, and unfortunately the Governor’s orders supersedes anything the City could do.
However, it does not negate the City’s attempt to spend 2 million dollars to provide a
subsidy to those that qualify or Inglewood renters. Mayor Butts, announced an
Emergency and recommended the Executive Order goes into effect immediately. Mayor
Butts asked if there was a motion.

It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
that the City Council does hereby adopt Executive Order No. 20-08 entitled:

  ORDER OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA EXTENDING
  EVICTION PROTECTIONS PROVIDED FOR IN EXECUTIVE ORDER 20-08
  TO JANUARY 21, 2021*

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
Noes: None.

* The mention of January 21st in the above matter referenced is incorrect. Pursuant to
State order (AB3088), which was signed by California Governor Newsom in August
2020, extended the Tenant Eviction Protections to January 31, 2021.
PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
